frontier.hypothesis: The last 13 of the 16 residual insns are one seat: b_src must land on $a0 instead of $v0, and since a priority lift cannot move it (v1), the only route is to create a CONFLICTING allocno that holds $v0 across b_src's live range - which is what the target has, since its $v0 carries all three channel sums.
frontier.mechanism: global.c find_reg gives an allocno the lowest-numbered hard register not in its conflict set. b_src (p128) spans combine insns 221..255 and conflicts with g_src (218..244) but with nothing holding $v0, so it takes 2. In the target, px dies at row 105 and b_src is defined at row 106 on the SAME register $a0, which is only reachable if 2 and 3 are both blocked for b_src at allocation time.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate source shapes that put a MULTI-referenced value in $v0 across rows 106-118 without adding an insn. w1's shared sum is the right allocno but the wrong live range (it spans all three channels and conflicts with r_src and g_src too); try instead a shared sum used for only the GREEN and BLUE channels, or a shared sum whose first def is after r_ch is consumed, and read the alloc table for a p13x allocno at hardreg 2 whose conflicts include p128 but not p123. Score only forms whose alloc row for p128 prints hardreg=4.

frontier.hypothesis: Both new levers are F1 chain extenders, so the 16 floor is currently FAKE-carrying; an ordinary-C carrier may exist for the g_src lift specifically, because its requirement is weak (any pricing above px's 32727, i.e. nrefs >= 14 at livelen 12) compared with the j lift's narrow (6111, 6964) window.
frontier.mechanism: pri = floor_log2(nrefs)*nrefs*10000/livelen. g_src at nrefs 14 / livelen 12 prices at 35000 > px's 32727, which is all the ordering needs - and unlike the j window there is no upper bound to respect, since px's pri is the only thing g_src must beat.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep ordinary-C spellings that give g_src one extra real reference at inner-loop depth 3 (weight +3 each), e.g. splitting g_ch = (g_sum >> 10) & 0x3E0 so g_src is read twice, deriving b_src from g_src's pre-shift value, or writing the green product as a compound assignment chain. Accept only forms with build_insns 173 whose alloc row for p126 prints pri > 32727 and hardreg=3.

frontier.hypothesis: The 3-insn trip-test residual (rows 127/128/130, target lh v0,4(s0) / lh v1,6(s0) / mult v0,v1 against ours lh v1 / lh v0 / mult v1,v0) is two locally-allocated temps named the other way round, and is decidable by the latch's expression shape.
frontier.mechanism: the two loads are short-lived pseudos that never reach the global allocno table (they are absent from the BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG rows), so local-alloc.c decides them from the order in which the quantities are born within the block.
frontier.next_probe: On the u3 chassis, sweep latch spellings that keep 173 insns and keep the slt shape: while (j < rect[2] * rect[3]) (current), a named local re-read per iteration, (s32)rect[2] * rect[3], and the product staged through the existing total variable re-assigned in the loop. Read rows 127-130 of the tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s21/sxs.py output, not the score alone.
